cards.explanation: The answer is a barber's razor. God tells Ezekiel to take a sharp sword and use it as a barber's razor to shave his head and beard (Ezekiel 5:1). A sword for a shave is a lot of trust in a steady hand, friends. I'd keep my mustache far away from that appointment.
The answer is scales. God says to take a set of scales and divide the hair (Ezekiel 5:1). Picture a prophet at the scales, sorting hair into three careful piles. That's a lot of focus for a haircut.

The answer is to slash it with the sword. God says to take a third and slash it with the sword all around the city (Ezekiel 5:2). The same sword that did the shaving now does the slashing. That's one busy sword for one sign.

The answer is True. God says to scatter a third to the wind, and adds, "For I will unleash a sword behind them." (Ezekiel 5:2) Burn one third, slash one third and scatter the last. Three piles, three different jobs.

The answer is fire. God says to take a few of these strands, throw them into the fire, and burn them (Ezekiel 5:4). They had been tucked safely in the folds of the garment, so it's a surprising turn. Even a few strands get a part to play.

The answer is to the whole house of Israel. A few strands are thrown into the fire, and "From there a fire will spread to the whole house of Israel." (Ezekiel 5:4) A handful of strands, and the reach is much bigger than the pile. That's a sobering picture, friends.

The answer is that she rebelled more wickedly than the nations did. God says Jerusalem "…has rebelled against My ordinances more wickedly than the nations…" (Ezekiel 5:6). She had been set in the center of the nations, with countries all around her (Ezekiel 5:5). That's a heavy thing to hear.

The answer is True, and it's a hard line. God says, "…nor have you even conformed to the ordinances of the nations around you." (Ezekiel 5:7) The nations had ordinances of their own. Jerusalem didn't live up to those either.

The answer is False. God says, "…I will execute judgments among you in the sight of the nations." (Ezekiel 5:8) The nations will see it. Later He says Jerusalem will be a ruin in the sight of all who pass by (Ezekiel 5:14).

The answer is what He has never done before. God says, "…I will do to you what I have never done before and will never do again." (Ezekiel 5:9) This is a heavy verse, friends. The reason He gives is all her abominations.

The answer is False. Because they defiled His sanctuary, God says He will withdraw His favor, and "I will not look upon you with pity, nor will I spare you." (Ezekiel 5:11) He says it as surely as He lives. It's a weighty word.

The answer is by plague or famine. The text says a third of the people "…will die by plague or be consumed by famine within you…" (Ezekiel 5:12). This is a heavy part, friends. I think it's one to read slowly.
The answer is the LORD. God says they "…will know that I, the LORD, in My zeal have spoken." (Ezekiel 5:13) It's His own word, spoken in His zeal. That's a heavy part, friends.

The answer is a warning and a horror. God says she will be "…a reproach and a taunt, a warning and a horror to the nations around you…" (Ezekiel 5:15). It's a hard picture, friends. It goes with Him executing judgments in anger, wrath, and raging fury.
The answer is True. God says, "I will send famine and wild beasts against you, and they will leave you childless." (Ezekiel 5:17) It's a heavy verse, friends. I think it's one to take slowly.
